title: Gravitational Lensing
definition: Gravitational lensing is a cosmic phenomenon where a massive celestial body (such as a galaxy cluster or black hole) causes a sufficient gravitational field to bend and distort the path of light traveling from a distant background source to an observer. It acts as a natural cosmic telescope, magnifying, distorting, or multiple-imaging distant objects.
importanceInUpsc: Tested frequently in UPSC Civil Services Prelims (Science & Tech / Astronomy) under space missions, astrophysics phenomena, and fundamental laws of physics (General Theory of Relativity), as well as in Mains GS-3 (Space technology, discoveries, and instrumentation).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Gravitational Lensing.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and cosmological applications.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity (1915)
Basic understanding of electromagnetic spectrum and cosmic structures
